blocks.title: After this PDF you can
bullets: express concession with por mucho que, por muy ... que, así, ni que
use indefinite forms (cualquiera que, quienquiera que, dondequiera que, sea lo que sea)
choose between indicative and subjunctive after quizá, tal vez, a lo mejor, puede que
use the subjunctive in fixed constructions (que yo sepa, no es que, sin que, el hecho de que)

head: Structure
Example
English
rows: Although he is tired, he goes on.
Even if he is tired, he will go on.
A pesar de que llovía, salimos.
Even though it was raining, we went out.
Por mucho que estudie, no aprueba.
However much he studies, he does not pass.
Por más que lo intento, no puedo.
However hard I try, I cannot.
Por muy caro que sea, lo compraré.
However expensive it is, I will buy it.
No lo haré, así me paguen.
I will not do it, even if they pay me.
As if you were rich! (you are not)
Si bien es caro, es bueno.
While it is expensive, it is good.

blocks.title: Known fact or not?
blocks.text: Aunque + indicative: the speaker accepts the fact. Aunque + subjunctive: not a fact, or the speaker does not care about it. Por mucho que + subjunctive is always subjunctive: the effort is open-ended.

head: Form
Example
English
rows: Cualquiera que sea la razón, lo haré.
Whatever the reason, I will do it.
Wherever you go, I will follow you.
Comoquiera que lo hagas, saldrá bien.
However you do it, it will turn out well.
Whatever it is, let me know.
Sea lo que sea, no cambiaré.
Whatever it is, I will not change.
One way or another, I will manage.
Pase lo que pase, estaré allí.
Whatever happens, I will be there.
Digan lo que digan, voy a ir.
Whatever they say, I am going.
Whether today or tomorrow, call me.
Ya sea por dinero o por amor, lo hará.
Whether for money or love, he will do it.

items: The pattern verb + lo que + same verb (subjunctive) means "whatever": pase lo que pase, haga lo que haga, digas lo que digas, pienses lo que pienses.
Cualquiera becomes cualquier before a noun: cualquier día, cualquier persona.

blocks.text: 3. Probability: quizá, tal vez, a lo mejor

head: Expression
Mood
Example
rows: indicative = more sure; subjunctive = less sure

blocks.title: A lo mejor
blocks.text: A lo mejor is the everyday way to say "maybe" in Spain. It never takes the subjunctive: A lo mejor no puede.

head: Expression
Example
English
rows: Que yo sepa, no ha llegado.
As far as I know, he has not arrived.
Que yo recuerde, nunca lo dijo.
As far as I remember, he never said it.
No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.
It is not that I do not want to, I cannot.
No lo hice porque me obligaran.
I did not do it because they forced me.
He left without us seeing him.
Con tal de que vengas, me da igual.
As long as you come, I do not mind.
El hecho de que llegue tarde me molesta.
The fact that he arrives late annoys me.
As long as you want, I will stay.
Cada vez que viene, trae flores.
Every time he comes, he brings flowers.
He had barely arrived when he left.
En cuanto a mí, estoy de acuerdo.

blocks.title: Fact with el hecho de que
blocks.text: Real facts normally take the indicative, but after el hecho de que Spanish uses the subjunctive when the speaker reacts to the fact: El hecho de que sea tu amigo no importa. The indicative is possible when the fact is simply informative: El hecho de que llegó tarde se notó.
5. Emotion, evaluation and denial (recap and extension)

head: Pattern
Example
English
rows: I am sorry you cannot come.
It surprises me that he knows so much.
I do not deny that he is right.
I deny that it is true.
no es verdad / cierto que + subj.
No es verdad que lo haya dicho.
It is not true that he said it.
It is obvious that he is right.
I fear he will arrive late.
Parece que llueve. / No parece que llueva.
It looks like rain. / It does not look like rain.
Por mucho que estudia, no aprueba.
Por mucho que estudie, no aprueba.
Que yo sé, no ha venido.
Que yo sepa, no ha venido.
Por muy cansado que esté, trabaja.
Repeat the verb in the subjunctive.

items.full: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.
Cada vez que viene, trae flores.

items.q: However hard I try, I cannot.
items.a: Por más que lo intento, no puedo.

items.q: Whatever happens, I will be there.
items.a: Pase lo que pase, estaré allí.
A lo mejor viene. / Quizá venga.

items.a: Que yo sepa, no ha llamado.
